dct_description_sm: The effects of prenatal exposure to polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and mercury (Hg) resulting from fish consumption were studied in fish eating populations from various countries. Prenatal exposure to PCBs and Hg have been linked to deficits in neurobehavioral development during infancy. However, neuromotor as well as neurophysiological effects at school age were studied in a limited number of studies. The purpose of this research was to examine the long-term consequences of prenatal exposure to environmental contaminants, especially PCBs, Hg and lead. This project was designed to extend previous findings by studying domains of effects that have been overlooked in many previous studies that could be related to learning difficulties and disabilities.
dct_subject_sm: Health sciences and contaminants -> Persistent organic pollutants (POPs)
Social sciences, economics and policy -> Inuit population
dct_title_s: Follow-up of Preschool-aged Children Exposed to PCBs and Mercury through Fish and Marine Mammal Consumption
